title: A method to implement the electrode-entropy differentiation for lithium batteries
author: Cho, Thenaisie, et al.

steps.title: Configure tester and chamber
steps.instruction: Connect the ARBIN LBT 21084 battery tester to the Jeio Tech IL‑11 temperature chamber and set the data acquisition parameters: sampling time 50 ms before filtering/down‑sampling and 1 s after, voltage resolution 0.01 mV, current resolution 0.1 mA, temperature resolution 0.25 °C.

steps.title: Perform CC‑CV cycling protocol
steps.instruction: Run 100 full charge‑discharge cycles using a constant‑current/constant‑voltage (CC‑CV) scheme between 3.0 V and 4.2 V at 0.75 C. During charge, switch to CV when 4.2 V is reached and terminate when the end‑of‑charge current falls to 50 mA. Discharge at 0.75 C to 3.0 V. Keep the chamber temperature at 45 °C throughout.

steps.title: Measure cell entropy potentiometrically
steps.instruction: Measure the cell entropy with the potentiometric method described in reference [4] and the implementation details given in the article’s “Implementation” section.

steps.title: Extract entropy profiles every 100 cycles
steps.instruction: After each block of 100 cycles, export the measured entropy profile for the cell.

steps.title: Resample entropy data with B‑spline
steps.instruction: For each extracted entropy profile, fit a degree‑3 B‑spline using the Python functions `splrep` and `splev` from `scipy.interpolate`. Resample the spline at every 1 % increment of state‑of‑charge (SOC) to obtain a uniform dataset.

steps.title: Compute entropy evolution ΔSevol
steps.instruction: Calculate the entropy evolution for each aging step n as ΔSevol,n(SOC) = ΔSfresh(SOC) − ΔSn(SOC), where ΔSfresh is the fresh‑cell entropy profile and ΔSn is the entropy profile after n cycles.

steps.title: Build 3‑D entropy evolution table
steps.instruction: Create a three‑dimensional table (cell × SOC × cycle number) that stores ΔSevol for every cell, SOC value, and aging step.

steps.title: Calculate cross‑correlation between cells
steps.instruction: For any pair of cells A and B, compute the cross‑correlation ρ at each SOC using ρ(ΔSevol,A,ΔSevol,B)(SOC) = ∑_{m=SOC}^{100‑SOC} ΔSevol,A(m)·ΔSevol,B(SOC+m). Use the Pearson correlation definition (Eq. 6) to verify symmetry and note that scaling constants α and β do not affect ρ.

steps.title: Conduct XRD material analysis
steps.instruction: Discharge the fresh cell to 3.0 V, disassemble it in an argon‑filled glove box, separate cathode and anode from the separator, wash each electrode in dimethyl carbonate (DMC), dry, and scrape with a sharp blade to obtain powder. Record X‑ray diffraction patterns from 2θ = 5° to 90° using CuKα1 radiation on a SmartLab (RIGAKU) diffractometer.

steps.title: Perform linear regression of entropy vs capacity loss
steps.instruction: Using the resampled entropy data, run a linear regression of ΔSevol versus capacity loss for each SOC point, extracting the slope and correlation coefficient for each cell.

steps.title: Evaluate normalized cross‑correlation thresholds
steps.instruction: Interpret normalized cross‑correlation values: consider ρ_norm > 0.65–0.8 as high correlation indicating similar electrode aging. Note that strong correlation is typically observed between 15 % and 50 % SOC, while values below 15 % SOC are unreliable due to chaotic entropy signals.
